Commentary.Commentary: ... THE RUN CHASE ...

A big chase for UAE - The United Arab Emirates now needs 194 runs to seal the victory. With the pitch in Chennai looking excellent for batting, the stage is set for a thrilling finish. The UAE openers will have to come out swinging and keep the scoreboard moving from ball one to stay ahead of the required run rate in this massive run chase.

Siddique shines with the ball - Despite the onslaught, the UAE bowlers kept fighting, led by the impressive Junaid Siddique. He was the standout performer with the ball, claiming 3 vital wickets to put the brakes on scoring during the death overs. His spell was crucial in preventing Italy from crossing the psychological 200-run mark.

Italy end their innings at 193/7! Italy has wrapped up their innings with a commanding score of 193/7 after 20 overs. The foundation was laid by a brilliant partnership between the Mosca brothers, with Anthony blasting a quick 56 and Justin supporting well with 48. A late, aggressive cameo from Grant Stewart ensured they finished on a high, setting a daunting task for the opposition.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set. The Mosca brothers have walked out to open for Italy as Justin Mosca and Anthony Mosca are out to open for Italy. Junaid Siddique is set to bowl the first ball of this contest.

Skipper of Italy - Harry Manenti says they were looking to bat first anyway. Mentions that the mood in the camp is positive as they have played good games against Ireland and Canada and they'll be looking to get a win today and head into the tournament on a high note.

Skipper of the United Arab Emirates - Waseem says that they'll be bowling first. Mentions that the game against Nepal was a good one, but they need to step up in the batting, as there is not much left before the World Cup.

United Arab Emirates - Muhammad Arfan, Haider Ali, Alishan Sharafu, Junaid Siddique, Muhammad Farooq, Muhammad Waseem (C), Mayank Kumar, Aryansh Sharma (WK), Dhruv Parashar, Muhammad Jawadullah, Muhammad Rohid, Simranjeet Singh, Muhammad Zohaib, Harshit Kaushik, Sohaib Khan.

Italy - Wayne Madsen, JJ Smuts, Gian-Piero Meade (WK), Benjamin Manenti, Grant Stewart, Crishan Kalugamage, Jaspreet Singh, Marcus Campopiano, Justin Mosca, Anthony Mosca, Harry Manenti, Ali Hasan, Syed Naqvi, Thomas Draca, Zain Ali.
TOSS​​​ - United Arab Emirates have won the toss and they have elected to BOWL first.

UAE tune up for a massive opening clash - UAE will be keen to iron out a few issues after their opening warm-up against Nepal, where Sohaib Khan, Harshit Kaushik and Aryansh Sharma helped them reach a competitive 145 but they could not make it count with the ball through the middle overs. There is also a sense that too much responsibility rests on the top order, something that could be exposed on a demanding Chepauk pitch unless the middle order steps up. With New Zealand waiting here in their World Cup opener, Muhammad Waseem's side will want this game to bring greater balance, tighter bowling and clearer roles as they finalise their plans. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

Italy looks to build on a winning start - Italy comes in with confidence after a competitive win over Canada that showed their ability to post a fighting total and defend it under pressure. JJ Smuts was at the heart of that performance with an important all-round contribution, while Harry Manenti and Justin Mosca added key runs in the middle and at the back end to give the innings shape. Their bowlers then showed enough control at the death to close the game out, and this match now offers another chance to fine-tune their balance and combinations ahead of the very different conditions that await later in the tournament.

Chepauk rehearsal with World Cup consequences - Italy and UAE step into a meaningful warm-up at the MA Chidambaram Stadium, Chennai, with far more at stake than just match practice. For UAE, this is the ideal rehearsal for their tournament opener against New Zealand at the same venue, on a surface that rewards discipline, smart spin and measured batting. Italy, meanwhile, are only briefly in Chennai before shifting to Eden Gardens for most of their group games, where the bounce and pace will be very different, making this clash an important test of their ability to adapt while still building winning momentum.
